writeup.headline: STMicroelectronics rates Hold: revenue is recovering and news is positive, but margins are thin and the shares are weak.
writeup.thesis: STM scores 51, a Hold, with growth, quality, trend and news risk carrying the weight because balance sheet and valuation were not scored. Growth scores 45. The company still shows a TTM revenue decline of 11.1%, but growth sped up by 12.2 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 56: gross margin is 33.9% and operating margin only 1.5%, offset by modest stock-based pay at 1.6% of revenue and a diluted share count down 1.7% year on year. Trend scores 43, with the price 39.3% below its 52-week high and shares 16.7 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, even though shares are up 111.0% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago. News risk is the strongest factor at 61, helped by a Q3 revenue beat of $3.76B, Q4 guidance of $4.15B at the midpoint and new automotive sensor launches.
key_risks: Operating margin of 1.5% leaves little room if the revenue recovery stalls.
Adjusted EPS missed estimates despite the revenue beat.
Weak price trend: the price is 3.7% below its 50-day average and 2.8% below its 200-day average.
A pending SDNY securities class action remains in the background.
Mixed analyst views, including a price target cut by TD Cowen.
what_would_change: A move up to Buy needs 14 more points, most likely from TTM revenue returning to growth and operating margin widening.
A drop of 7 points would mean Sell, which could follow if the price trend weakens further or guidance disappoints.
A balance sheet or valuation score, once available, could move the composite in either direction; cash is 1.79 times debt.
Delivering Q4 revenue near the $4.15B guidance midpoint would support both the growth and news factors.
